texts.facts: The petitioners have challenged the impugned notification, dated 25.10.2018, published in Daily Thanthi under Section 3A (1) of the National Highways Act 1956 issued by the Competent Authority/Special District Revenue Officer (Land Acquisition), National Highways No.45-A, District Collectorate, Villupuram, 3rd respondent herein, in so far as their lands are concerned and consequently, prayed for a direction to the Competent Authority/Special District Revenue Officer (Land Acquisition), National Highways No.45-A, District Collectorate, Villupuram and the District Collector, Villupuram District, District Collectorate, Villupuram, respondents 3 and 4 herein, to constitute a committee of experts to study and Jayaraman vs The Chairman on 30 July, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/94308336/ 2 formulate, a report suggesting alternative alignment, by protecting the lands of the petitioners. 2. It is the case of the petitioners that they are agriculturists, having lands in Kengarampalayam Village, Villupuram District. Out of the said lands, the 3rd respondent has sought to acquire lands, on behalf of the respondents 1 and 2 under the provisions of National Highways Act, for widening the existing Highway for formation of four lane in National http://www.judis.nic.in Highways No.45-A (New No. 332A) connecting Chennai and Nagapattinam on South Eastern Post Corridor of Tamil Nadu of the 185 Km stretch connecting Villupuram to Nagapattinam through major state and towns namely, Puducherry, Cuddalore, Chidambaram and Sirgazhi, it would be implemented in 4 phaces and it is expected to be completed in 2 years, from the commencement of the work by the end of February 2019. 3. In the meantime, National Highways Authority had issued notifications recently, to acquire additional land of 107.2644 Hectors under the National Highways Act for the project in Kancheepuram District, the project aims to improve the traffic movements along the South Eastern Coast and facilitate free movement of heavy vehicles to ports in Karaikal and Chennai, besides bringing down the travel time and ensuring a smooth ride for the road users travelling from East Coast Corridor to the State Capital namely Chennai to Nagapattinam and vice versa. 4. The petitioner has further submitted that as per the letter in Ref.No.1101/NH-45A/12/PIU VPM/2019/152, dated 19.01.2019, addressed the National Highways Authority of India, to the competent authority and http://www.judis.nic.in Special District Revenue Officer (LA) National Highways 45A, Villupuram, had made a request to proceed for acquisition of additional lands (extent of land 5 times more than the lands already acquired) apart from the project of widening of National Four Lane Highways and for the other proposed projects such as Highway rest area, and Toll Plaza along the corridor. Furthermore, the location of the Highways Rest area and Toll Plaza has been identified in Gengarampalayam Village, for which, additional lands of the petitioners are required to be acquired. 5. The Competent Authority/Special District Revenue Officer (Land Acquisition), National Highways No.45-A, District Collectorate, Villupuram, 3rd respondent herein, published a notification in Daily Thanthi newspaper Cuddalore edition, dated 12.10.2018 and 25.10.2018 under Section 3-A(l) of the National Highways Act, 1956 to acquire additional lands for widening the existing road and for other facilities such as, rest area and Toll Plaza proposed along the Corridor for which additional lands are acquired in Gangarampalayam Village in the National Highways 45-A. According to the petitioners, no notification was published in any of the Tamil daily newspapers which is in circulation of Villupuram District edition, with the malafide intention to forebear the http://www.judis.nic.in petitioners from knowing about the additional land acquisition proceedings. Pursuant to the said notification, the petitioners and others submitted their common objections to the 3rd respondent on various dates and lastly on 25.2.2019. The petitioners uniformly made the objections including the necessity of acquisition of land by re-aligning the Highways road, which would cause irreparable loss and damage to the general public as well as the agriculturists and their agricultural lands. Jayaraman vs The Chairman on 30 July, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/94308336/ 3 6. During the year 2014-2015, a survey was done at the instance of respondents 1 and 2 by the District Collector, Villupuram, 4th respondent for formation of bye-pass road near Bhuvanagiri-Mutlur, in the existing road and the said survey was on straight line, without affecting any residential area with intention to minimise the land acquisition. Minimising the acquisition of land, resulted in deduction of expenditure, in convenience caused to the public less traffic problem with clear view of road, enabling the transport vehicle to pass easily without any accident and to save the agricultural operation in the said area. The general public including the petitioners were under the impression as informed by the authorities that the said survey would be the final one, for formation of four-lane Highway. http://www.judis.nic.in 7. Contrary to the assurance and in order to favour certain individuals for exclusion of their lands, another survey was made on 24.05.2016 and 25.05.2016 respectively, despite objections made by the residents. The above survey was made by outsourcing an agency, outside the State of Tamil Nadu, who does not practically know about the geographical location of the subject area and dislocation of the residences. The said survey would affect 80% of the residential area of Gangarampalayam Village. The said survey would also affect the agricultural activities and also lead to flood during rainy season. According to them, the proposed road, if formed as per the said survey of the year 2016, it will give way for many accidents and it would make the subject area as accident prone zone. The ultimate sufferers are the villagers and general public who would lose their life and shelter. Moreover, some people have received compensation for the already existing road route for formation of four lanes. 8. The petitioners have further submitted that two resolutions were passed by the Panchayat Board of Gangarampalaym Village Panchayat, on 23.01.2015 and 27.05.2016 respectively, requesting to retain the existing road route for formation of four land based on 2015 http://www.judis.nic.in Survey instead of new route based on the survey done in the year 2016. The Panchayat Board through the said resolutions expressed its strong objections to the new alignment by referring to the agony that would be caused to the public and requested the District Collector to form the additional lane on the existing road instead of making a diversion. But, the same are not considered, despite the representation was forwarded by the office of the Honble Minister of Road Transport, Highways and Shipping, Government of India on 30.07.2016. On 15.08.2018, resolutions were passed by the Panchayat Board of M.N.Kuppam and Gangarampalaym, expressing their strong objections and requested the District Collector to form the additional lane on the existing road instead of making diversion. 9. The petitioners have further submitted that the affected land owners numbering 105, including the petitioners have jointly made a representation on 25.2.2019 to the respondents and other higher Jayaraman vs The Chairman on 30 July, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/94308336/ 4 officials and top bureaucrats of the National Highways Road and Transport Department. It was not considered and no peace committee meeting was held. However, it was assured by the officials that they would not implement the objected alignment and that they would adopt only the http://www.judis.nic.in original alignment. But contrary to the said assurance and without properly considering the bonafide and legitimate objections of the petitioners and other land owners, the respondents proceed to acquire additional land by adopting the newly surveyed alignment, which is totally adverse to the interest of the public and also affect the land owners including the petitioners heavily. 10. It is the further case of the petitioners that a larger extent of land Poramboke lands (lands which are not assessed to revenue records and it is outside the revenue records) and Temple lands are located adjacent/adjoining to the proposed acquisition of additional lands and so there are ample possibilities of alternative measures of shifting the construction and formation of Highway rest area and Toll Plaza by adopting re-alignment process. The aforesaid lands are comprised in R.S.No. 98, 171, 142/1, 142/2 and 100 of the same village and for better self serving demonstration and for illustration, the copy of FMD sketch is filed. Their valid and reasonable objections, dated 25.02.2019 have not been considered, due to application of mind of the authorities concerned. The decision of the competent authority violates the provisions of Section 3C of the Act and resultantly, all subsequent proceedings stand vitiated. http://www.judis.nic.in 11. The petitioners have further submitted that some of the affected individuals filed a writ petition in W.P.No.27963 of 2017, for issuance of a Writ of Certiorarified Mandamus to call for the records pertinent to the notification dated 08.07.2017 issued by the 3rd respondent published in Tamil news paper Thinathanthi for acquisition of lands. This Court was pleased to admit the above writ petition and also granted an order of injunction on 09.01.2018. Subsequently, the said interim order was extended on 07.02.2018 by this Court and thereafter the writ petition has been disposed of with a direction to consider the petitioners grievances and to pass an appropriate orders and also in W.P.No.6705 of 2017, interim order has granted on 21.03.2019. Pending the above writ petition, the respondents herein are proceeding with the land acquisition by issuing notice under Section 3 (A) of the National Highways Act, called upon the petitioners and others to attend an enquiry to be held on 25.02.2019 at 11.00 am in the office of the Special District Revenue Officer (LA) National Highway-45A, Room No.8, District collector Campus, Villupuram. Since they have not filed any writ petition, similar to the writ petition filed by others, subordinates of the respondents caused a threat on the petitioners that their lands will be taken possession in absence of any injunction order granted in their favour. In http://www.judis.nic.in view of the above, the petitioners have filed this writ petition, on the following grounds, (i) The impugned notification published in Daily Thanthi Tamil Newspaper, Cuddalore edition dated 12.10.2018 and 25.10.2018 purported to be issued under Section 3A(1) of the National Highways Act, 1956 issued by the 3rd respondent suffers from illegalities, irregularities and in excess of jurisdiction. Jayaraman vs The Chairman on 30 July, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/94308336/ 5 (ii) The respondents ought not to have re-aligned the existing road and introduce a new way by formation of new four line road is contrary to the original notification issued by the 3rd respondent with a malafide intention to favour few individuals whose properties will be acquired if the original alignment is executed. The said approach of the respondents vitiates the entire land acquisition proceedings under the National Highways Act. The objection petitions were invited in accordance with section 3C of NH Act 1956 from the land owner/ interested persons, if any, within 21 days from the date of publication of 3A(1) Notification made in the local newspapers on 25.10.2018. xi. xii. On receipt of technical opinion of the Project Director, the 3rd respondent has issued notices to all the objection petitioners and requested vide communication dated 01.02.2019 to appear for enquiry on 25.02.2019 under section 3C (2) NH Act 1956. They orally represented their objection to the acquisition of their lands and disbursed after some time. 4. Third respondent furnished a proposal dated 12.10.2018 and requested to publish the same in local newspaper under section 3A(3) of NH Act. The petitioners are put to strict proof of their allegation. The petitioners have filed objections before the 3rd respondent and Competent Authority http://www.judis.nic.in and Special District Revenue Officer, Land Acquisition, Villupuram. The 3rd respondent has issued notice to the land owners and requested to appear before the Competent Authority / SDRO on 25.02.2019.
texts.arguments: (iii) The respondents have failed to note that there was no consultation with the public or the land owners or the elected representative prior to finalizing the new route alignment which caused heavy monetary loss and irreparable loss to the land owners besides life of the general public using the said National Highway which has several dangerous curves result in more accidents. The non-consideration of the said facts vitiates the entire notification itself. (iv) The respondents have failed to note that it is totally an empty formality to call for objection after http://www.judis.nic.in finalizing the route/alignment in the absence of aggrieved land owners. Hence, the very impugned notification calling for objections are arbitrary, unreasonable, unilateral, contrary to land acquisition procedure and unsustainable both under law and facts besides that unacceptable and against the interest of the land owners and agriculturists whose property right has been infringed despite of Constitutional safeguard provided them. (v) The respondents have failed to follow the established procedure on the part of NHAI that the expansion of road shall be done along the existing road and not laying the new road adjacent to the existing road but the said norms has not been followed by the respondents for an ulterior motive at the cost of the Central and State Government Funds. (vi) The expert team, which was engaged by the NHAI has not done its work of choosing the alignment in its best way. 12. The petitioners have further submitted that the respondents are proceedings with the acquisition, despite the pendency of earlier writ petition before this Court. By grant of stay no prejudice would cause to the respondents. On the other hand if no stay is granted, the petitioners would be put into irreparable loss and hardship besides http://www.judis.nic.in multiplicity of proceedings. It is submitted that the project alignment in Gangarampalayam village is proposed along the existing NH only, since the existing NH is in straight line as well as in order to utilize the existing ROW. The existing ROW of about 22m to 30m is being utilized for this project to avoid new acquisition in the adjoining agricultural land. Hence, it is submitted that due consideration was given to minimize the acquisition of agricultural land on both sides. Totally 88 Nos. of buildings such as houses, shops & religious structures are getting affected due to the acquisition of 45m ROW. In respect of the additional land acquisition for Toll plaza, only 4 buildings are getting affected and 51 buildings in the additional acquisition are getting affected in the widening portion. It is settled law that the Honble Court will not interfere in the technical alignment unless there is a clear case of mala fide or it is found to be ex-forcie contrary to the mandate of law. It is submitted that the alignment was neither changed nor modified in Gangarampalayam village as alleged by the Petitioner in para 6. The aforesaid allegation is totally false and untrue and therefore this bald plea is liable to rejected. This project alignment utilizes the existing RoW of 22m to 30m in the stretch and hence, minimizes the acquisition of adjacent agricultural lands. The project alignment is very straight in this stretch and four lane carriage way is being proposed which would ultimately avoid the accidents. The petitioner has mentioned that the said survey could also affect the agricultural activities and also lead to flood during rainy seasons. It is submitted that the consultant has examined all criteria and also ascertained that this stretch exist away from the risk of http://www.judis.nic.in flooding and submergence during the rainy season. Hence, as per the prevailing law of the land, the averments against the alignment made by the petitioner are not sustainable and liable to be dismissed. 8. With regard to averments made by the petitioner in para 8 of the affidavit, respondents 1 and 2 have submitted that the petitioner has stated that two resolutions was passed by panchayat board of Gangarampalayam on 23.10.2015 and 27.05.2016 requesting to retain the existing road route for formation of four lane road based on 2015 survey instead of new route based on the survey done on 2016. This averments made by the petitioner in para 8 is strongly denied and submitted that there is no change of alignment proposed by the consultant in the stretch of Gangarampalayam village. It is further stated that to the best of knowledge and belief of the Respondent, no such resolutions were passed by the said panchayat and sent to the 2nd Respondent. Determination of alignment is the function of technical experts based on technical criteria. The alignment is taken through the existing NH only for which the LA notifications were published since 2014. It is submitted that the additional land for Toll plaza was also notified under the section 3A(1) of NH Act in Gangarampalayam village is in respect of the same alignment only without any alteration and deviations. The land owners have orally expressed their objections for the acquisition of additional land for the Toll plaza. It is submitted that the alignment originally proposed while acquiring 45m ROW has not been changed. The same alignment is being followed for acquisition of additional land for Toll plaza also. It is submitted that neither the alignment was modified nor any assurance was given to the public. The petitioners are put to strict proof of the unfounded plea of assurance. Thus, the averments made in para 9 are not tenable and is liable to be dismissed. The petitioner has alleged that the project alignment did not utilize the Government land exist in survey number 98, 171, 142/1, 142/2 and 100 in the Gangarampalayam village. This allegation is strongly denied and submitted that the Government land to an extent of 908 sqm in Survey numbers http://www.judis.nic.in Jayaraman vs The Chairman on 30 July, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/94308336/ 13 no.98, 54 sqm in Survey numbers 142/1, 43 sq.mt.in survey number 142/2, 886 sqm in Survey number 100/1 are being utilized for. Further, an extent of 2575 sq.mt. in survey number 171 was also acquired in the private land. Apart from the above, the Government land to an extent of 4567 sqm is also utilized for this project in Gangarampalayam village. Thus the averments made in para 10 do not deserve any consideration and are liable to be dismissed. It is submitted that the petitioners of the above writ petitions have objected to the formation of Bypass alignment for the B. Mutlur village and demanded to fix the alignment along the existing NH only. It is submitted that the demand of those writ petitioners cannot be accepted since where around 200 Nos. of building such as houses and shops etc., will be affected if the alignment is taken through the existing NH. Those writ petitioners propose an entirely a new alignment which is technically not feasible of compliance. On the other hand, in the instant Writ petition, the petitioners have objected for the project alignment through existing NH where 85 Nos. of buildings such as houses, shops & religious structures are getting affected. Moreover, since the Toll plaza has to be located in a straight stretch of the existing http://www.judis.nic.in NH only, Realignment may not be proposed in Gangarampalayam village. It is submitted that as per the policy circular and standard norms, a Toll plaza shall be located only in the existing NH not in the bypass alignment. The total length of the project is about 29 km in which the bypass alignment accounts to 16.35 km. The Toll plaza has to be located in the project alignment proposed along the existing NH between km.16/350 to km.29/000. The location of Toll plaza shall be identified in such a way that there shall be straight stretch of NH of not less than 1 km, away from Municipal limits and there shall not be any leakage roads which may hamper the Toll revenue after completion of the project. Accordingly, the location of Toll plaza has been proposed in km. 18/500 in Gangarampalayam village. It is not correct for the petitioners to level unfounded and baseless allegations against the Respondents that they have taken possession of Jayaraman vs The Chairman on 30 July, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/94308336/ 14 land owners who have not filed writ petition. The Petitioners are put to strict proof of the same. Thus the averments made in para 12 are not related to this package-1 and do not have any legal force and are liable to be dismissed straight away. The writ petitioners allegation that the Respondents are adopting the new alignment as against the original alignment with a mala fide intention to favour few individuals is baseless and a imaginary product of wild conjecture and totally against the facts and the petitioners are bound to prove the above wild allegations. Further, the contentions of the writ petitioners are opposed to facts and law and the Respondents are legally competent to acquire the lands for the purpose of development, management, maintenance and operation of the National Highways under the National Highways Act, 1956. Further, law is well settled that, under the Doctrine of Eminent Domain, the Government of India is entitled to acquire the Private lands for the public purpose of laying the National Highways. Therefore, the averments raised in the ground do not merit any consideration and are liable to be dismissed as devoid of any legal substance. The writ petitioners allegation are not supported either by law or by facts. Hence, it is liable to he dismissed. It is further submitted that right to properly is not a http://www.judis.nic.in fundamental right. In a catena of decisions, the Hon'ble Supreme Court has already held that when private lands are acquired by the State for public purpose under the doctrine of Eminent Domain no plea of fundamental right can be advanced against it since public welfare is superior to private right. Hence the contention is liable for outright dismissal. In this acquisition, fundamental rights of the people will not be affected and the land owners will be eligible to get fair compensation as per the provisions of RFCTLARR Act 2013 though Land Acquisition proceedings are carried out under the NH Act 1956. The alleged apprehension of Jayaraman vs The Chairman on 30 July, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/94308336/ 17 imminent threat and danger of dispossession is baseless and unfounded and hence the contention is liable to be rejected as devoid of any legal merit. 15. In S.Joel Versus Union Government of India, (in WP.No.29839 of 2010, dated 20.04.2015), the Division Bench of this Court, held as follows: It is settled legal position that this Court exercising power of judicial review would not interfere with the decision or discretion exercised by an authority, unless it is shown that the decision was wholly arbitrary and actuated by bias and mala fides. In the case on hand, the petitioner has not alleged any bias or malafide, but would state Jayaraman vs The Chairman on 30 July, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/94308336/ 19 that the action of the respondent in shifting the Toll Plaza to the present location amounts to malice in law. This argument steams out of the proposition advocated by the petitioner that the relocation of the second Toll Plaza contravenes Rule http://www.judis.nic.in 8 o f the Rules. In the preceding paragraphs, we are out rightly rejected such contentions raised by the petitioner and held that the Rule 8 would have no application to the facts of the present case. On this http://www.judis.nic.in aspect, we are in respectful agreement with the decision of the Madhya Pradesh High Court in the case of Manish Jaiswal & Anr., (supra), as pointed out therein the decision with regard to location of the Toll Plaza has been arrived at by the experts after taking into account, the relevant factors mentioned in the agreement and the fixation of alignment and identification o f the spot for location of Toll Plaza are the matters within the domain of the authority mentioned in the agreement and this Court in the proceedings under Article 226, cannot sit in appeal over the decision of fixation of the alignment and the identification of the spot for locating the Toll Plaza and therefore, it is better to leave the decision to experts, who are familiar with the issue to decide the location of Toll Plaza" 16. The Honble Supreme Court in Ramniklal N. Bhutta and Another vs. State Of Maharashtra & Ors (1997(1) SCC 134) while dealing with the challenge made to the acquisition proceeding initiated under NH Act, 1956, held as follows: Before parting with this case, we think it necessary to make a few observations relevant to land acquisition proceedings. Our country is now launched upon an ambitious programme of all-round economic advancement to make our economy competitive in the world market. We are anxious to attract foreign direct investment to the maximum extent. 17. The Honble Supreme Court in Union o f India Vs. Dr. Kushala Shetty & Ors reported in 2011(12) SCC 69, at Paragraph 24, held as follows: 4. Moreover, since the Toll plaza has to be located in a straight stretch of the existing http://www.judis.nic.in NH only, Realignment may not be proposed in Gangarampalayam village. It is submitted that as per the policy circular and standard norms, a Toll plaza shall be located only in the existing NH not in the bypass alignment. The total length of the project is about 29 km in which the bypass alignment accounts to 16.35 km. The Toll plaza has to be located in the project alignment proposed along the existing NH between km.16/350 to km.29/000. The location of Toll plaza shall be identified in such a way that there shall be straight stretch of NH of not less than 1 km, away from Municipal limits and there shall not be any leakage roads which may hamper the Toll revenue after completion of the project. Accordingly, the location of Toll plaza has been proposed in km. 18/500 in Gangarampalayam village. It is not correct for the petitioners to level unfounded and baseless allegations against the Respondents that they have taken possession of Jayaraman vs The Chairman on 30 July, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/94308336/ 14 land owners who have not filed writ petition. The Petitioners are put to strict proof of the same. Thus the averments made in para 12 are not related to this package-1 and do not have any legal force and are liable to be dismissed straight away. The writ petitioners allegation that the Respondents are adopting the new alignment as against the original alignment with a mala fide intention to favour few individuals is baseless and a imaginary product of wild conjecture and totally against the facts and the petitioners are bound to prove the above wild allegations. Therefore, the averments raised in the ground do not merit any consideration and are liable to be dismissed as devoid of any legal substance. The writ petitioners allegation are not supported either by law or by facts. Hence, it is liable to he dismissed. In a catena of decisions, the Hon'ble Supreme Court has already held that when private lands are acquired by the State for public purpose under the doctrine of Eminent Domain no plea of fundamental right can be advanced against it since public welfare is superior to private right. Hence the contention is liable for outright dismissal. In this acquisition, fundamental rights of the people will not be affected and the land owners will be eligible to get fair compensation as per the provisions of RFCTLARR Act 2013 though Land Acquisition proceedings are carried out under the NH Act 1956. The alleged apprehension of Jayaraman vs The Chairman on 30 July, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/94308336/ 17 imminent threat and danger of dispossession is baseless and unfounded and hence the contention is liable to be rejected as devoid of any legal merit. This argument steams out of the proposition advocated by the petitioner that the relocation of the second Toll Plaza contravenes Rule http://www.judis.nic.in 8 o f the Rules. In the preceding paragraphs, we are out rightly rejected such contentions raised by the petitioner and held that the Rule 8 would have no application to the facts of the present case.

On this http://www.judis.nic.in aspect, we are in respectful agreement with the decision of the Madhya Pradesh High Court in the case of Manish Jaiswal & Anr., (supra), as pointed out therein the decision with regard to location of the Toll Plaza has been arrived at by the experts after taking into account, the relevant factors mentioned in the agreement and the fixation of alignment and identification o f the spot for location of Toll Plaza are the matters within the domain of the authority mentioned in the agreement and this Court in the proceedings under Article 226, cannot sit in appeal over the decision of fixation of the alignment and the identification of the spot for locating the Toll Plaza and therefore, it is better to leave the decision to experts, who are familiar with the issue to decide the location of Toll Plaza" 16.
